# What You Will Build

*One product, one page, and a fluffy cat that follows your cursor. Everything you need is in this guide, ready to copy and paste.*

❦

This guide walks you through building a one-product website for a cat food brand called Mochi. The hero is a cartoon cat that looks wherever your mouse goes. Below it, smooth scroll animations sell the product from every angle. See the finished site at [mochi-cat-food.vercel.app](https://mochi-cat-food.vercel.app).

| PART OF THE PAGE | WHAT IT DOES |
| :---- | :---- |
| Hero | A fluffy white cat on a hot pink background looks toward your cursor. The headline "Picky eaters, / clean bowls." sits on either side of it. |
| The bag | A kitten hugging the product bag (a looping video), kibble floating around it, price, subscribe or one-time, quantity and "Add to bag". |
| What's inside | The bag floating among flying kibble (a looping video), big stats with hand-drawn arrows, ingredients and nutrition. |
| How much to feed | A cat eating from a bowl, a feeding calculator and a closing "buy" banner. |
| Motion | Smooth scrolling, words rising in, photos unmasking, the hero shrinking into a card, crossing ribbons, a circular reveal and a kibble burst. |

## The full pipeline

* Find a reference cat on Pinterest and turn it into a clean studio image with ChatGPT

* Animate only the cat's eyes with Google Flow

* Generate 5 product photos with GPT Image 2 on Kie AI, each one using the bag as its reference

* Generate 2 short product videos with Kling 2.6 on Kie AI and loop them with FFmpeg

* Build the whole website with one master prompt in Claude Code

* Test it on your computer, then put it live with GitHub and Vercel

## How to copy from this guide

You never have to write a prompt or a line of code. There are two kinds of copy box:

| Prompt box Light pink. Paste into an AI tool: ChatGPT, Google Flow, Kie AI or Claude Code. The label above the box names the tool. |  | Terminal box Dark plum. Paste into Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell (Windows) inside your project folder, then press Enter. |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |

| 💡  Triple-click anywhere inside a box to select the whole prompt or command in one go, then copy with Cmd+C (Mac) or Ctrl+C (Windows). Each box is a single paragraph, so nothing gets left behind and nothing extra comes with it. |

# Make the Hero Cat Video

*This is the cat that follows the cursor. Find a style reference, turn it into a clean studio image, then animate only the eyes.*

❦

## 2.1  Find a reference on Pinterest

Search Pinterest and save one picture you love. You only use it as a style reference, so it does not need to be perfect.

COPY THIS PROMPT   *paste into the Pinterest search bar*

| cute fluffy white kitten 3D Pixar style |
| :---- |

## 2.2  Turn it into a clean landscape hero image

1. Open ChatGPT and start a new chat.

2. Upload your Pinterest picture.

3. Paste the prompt below and send it.

4. Download the result and save it in your project folder as `hero-image.png`.

COPY THIS PROMPT   *paste into ChatGPT*

| Use the cat from the uploaded image as the character reference. Keep the same character design, face, fur colour, eye colour and style.Create a 16:9 landscape image (1920×1080). The cat sits upright, full body visible from ear tips to paws, centred horizontally, facing the camera and looking straight at the viewer with big open eyes.Paws together in front of its chest.Background: a seamless hot pink studio backdrop (\#EC2F69), slightly darker at the top corners, with a soft lighter pink floor. Soft, even studio lighting. No props, no text, nothing else in the frame.Leave clear empty space on the left and right of the cat for website headline text. |
| :---- |

![Expected hero image][image20]

*Your result should look like this: the cat centred, with empty pink space on both sides.*

| ⚠️  The cat must be centred with empty space on the left and right. The website puts the headline there. Keep the background plain; the site colours are matched to it. |
| :---- |

## 2.3  Animate the eyes in Google Flow

1. Open Google Flow and create a new video from an image.

2. Upload `hero-image.png` as the start frame.

3. Paste the prompt below and generate.

4. Download the result as MP4 (a 6 to 8 second clip).

5. Rename it `hero-cat.mp4` and move it into your project folder.

COPY THIS PROMPT   *paste into Google Flow*

| Use the exact same cat from the uploaded reference image. Do not change or recreate the character in any way.Make the cat look in five directions using ONLY its eyes:Left → Right → Top → Bottom → CenterThe cat must remain in the exact same position throughout the entire animation.The head must NOT move, turn, tilt, rotate, or change position. The body must NOT move. Only the pupils/eyes should move.Keep everything else completely identical to the reference image:\- Exact same cat and character design\- Exact same face and facial expression\- Exact same head position and angle\- Exact same body position\- Exact same paws and feet\- Exact same size and proportions\- Exact same white fluffy fur\- Exact same pink gradient background\- Exact same lighting\- Exact same camera position and framingEye movement sequence:1\. Eyes look LEFT2\. Eyes look RIGHT3\. Eyes look UP4\. Eyes look DOWN5\. Eyes return to CENTERMake each eye movement clear, smooth and controlled, with a short pause at each direction.Absolutely no head movement. No body movement. No camera movement. No blinking. No mouth movement. No ear movement. No facial deformation. No character morphing. No background movement.Only animate the eyes. Everything else must remain perfectly frozen and pixel-consistent with the uploaded reference image.This animation will be used for a cursor-tracking website hero, so the five eye directions need to be visually distinct and easy to map to cursor position. |
| :---- |

### What the video model actually gives you

Video models do not always obey. Our cat still moved its head a little and blinked between directions. That is fine: the website analyses every frame and picks the one that matches the cursor.

| YOUR VIDEO | WHAT THE SITE DOES | HOW SMOOTH |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| One slow, continuous sweep, far left to far right, no blinks | Scrubs the video like a slider as the mouse moves | Very smooth |
| Several held poses with blinks between them (most tools) | Jumps to the best-matching frame with a quick crossfade | Good, small jumps |

Want the smoothest result? Generate again with this prompt instead:

COPY THIS PROMPT   *paste into Google Flow (optional)*

| Use the exact same cat from the uploaded image. Locked camera. The cat slowly turns its head and eyes in one continuous, even movement from looking far LEFT to looking far RIGHT over the whole clip. No pauses, no blinking, no cuts, no zoom. Everything else stays identical: same cat, same pose, same pink background, same lighting and framing. |
| :---- |

| ⚠️  The video must be H.264 MP4. Some tools export HEVC (H.265), which Chrome cannot play. If the video shows nothing in Chrome, run the command below. Replace `input.mp4` with the name of the file you downloaded. |
| :---- |

TERMINAL   *only if the video will not play*

| `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 18 -movflags +faststart -an hero-cat.mp4` |
| :---- |

## 3.6  Option B: make all five automatically with Kie AI

Skip this if you already made the images by hand. The script makes the bag first, uploads it, then uses it as the reference for the other scenes.

1. Create an account at kie.ai and copy your API key.

2. Save the key in a file called `.env.local`. Paste this, with your real key in place of the placeholder:

TERMINAL   *paste into Terminal, then press Enter*

| `echo "KIE_API_KEY=paste-your-key-here" > .env.local` |
| :---- |

| ⚠️  Never share `.env.local` or upload it to GitHub. It holds your paid API key. |
| :---- |

3. In VS Code, create the file `scripts/generate-images.mjs` and paste the full script from Appendix A.

4. Run it:

TERMINAL   *paste into Terminal, then press Enter*

| `node scripts/generate-images.mjs              # makes all 5 (skips ones already made)node scripts/generate-images.mjs --only kitten-hug --force   # remake just one` |
| :---- |

### How the Kie AI API works (for reference)

Every request sends the header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY`.

| WHAT | REQUEST |
| :---- | :---- |
| Create an image | `POST https://api.kie.ai/api/v1/jobs/createTask` with model `gpt-image-2-text-to-image` |
| Image with a reference | Same URL, model `gpt-image-2-image-to-image`, plus `input_urls` with the bag image URL |
| Upload your reference | `POST https://kieai.redpandaai.co/api/file-stream-upload`, returns `data.fileUrl` |
| Check if it is done | `GET https://api.kie.ai/api/v1/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=...` until `data.state` is `success` |

| ⚠️  Kie gotchas we hit: image-to-image rejects the 4:5 ratio, so use 3:4. The `background` option only works at 1K; leave it out for 2K images. |
| :---- |

## 4.3  Make the videos loop without a jump

A 5-second clip jumps when it restarts. This plays each clip forward, then backward, so the end meets the start. It also shrinks the files for the web (about 0.7 MB and 1.2 MB).

TERMINAL   *paste into Terminal, then press Enter*

| `mkdir -p public/videosfor n in kitten-hug pouch-float; do  ffmpeg -y -i video-sources/$n.mp4 -filter_complex \    "[0:v]scale=900:-2:flags=lanczos,split[a][b];[b]reverse,trim=start_frame=1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[r];[a][r]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0,format=yuv420p[v]" \    -map "[v]" -an -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 25 -profile:v high -movflags +faststart public/videos/$n.mp4done` |
| :---- |

 

—   STEP 5   —

# Shrink and Organise the Files

*Raw PNGs are 2 to 6 MB each. As WebP they are 20 to 120 KB and look the same.*

❦

| 💡  The master prompt in Step 6 also does this conversion. Run it yourself when you want to check the files first, or skip straight to Step 6\. |
| :---- |

## 5.1  Convert the photos to WebP

TERMINAL   *paste into Terminal, then press Enter*

| `mkdir -p public/imagespython3 - <<'EOF'from PIL import Image# photos: resize and compressfor name, width in [('kitten-hug', 1200), ('pouch-float', 1200), ('cat-bowl', 1600)]:    im = Image.open(f'image-sources/{name}.png').convert('RGB')    im.thumbnail((width, width * 2), Image.LANCZOS)    im.save(f'public/images/{name}.webp', 'WEBP', quality=80, method=6)# cutouts: keep transparency, trim empty edgesfor name, width in [('pouch', 800), ('kibble', 600)]:    im = Image.open(f'image-sources/{name}.png').convert('RGBA')    im = im.crop(im.getbbox())    im.thumbnail((width, width * 2))    im.save(f'public/images/{name}.webp', 'WEBP', quality=86, method=6)EOF` |
| :---- |

The three single kibble pieces (`kibble-one`, `kibble-two`, `kibble-three`) are cut out of `kibble.png` automatically by the master prompt.

## 5.2  Keep the big originals off GitHub

FILE   *paste into .gitignore*

—   STEP 6   —

# Build the Website With One Prompt

*One master prompt builds everything: the project, the cursor-tracking hero, every section, the animations, and a final check in a real browser.*

❦

## 6.1  Before you paste

Check your project folder has these files:

* `hero-cat.mp4` in the main folder

* Five PNGs in `image-sources`: pouch, kitten-hug, pouch-float, cat-bowl, kibble

* Two MP4s in `video-sources`: kitten-hug, pouch-float

| 💡  Building for your own brand? Before pasting, change the brand name (Mochi), product name (Mochi Crunch), prices (\$22.49 and \$24.99), ingredients, nutrition numbers and colours. The values in the prompt are examples. |
| :---- |

## 6.2  Run it

1. Open your `mochi-cat-food` folder in VS Code.

2. Start Claude Code: click the Claude icon in the side bar, or type `claude` in the VS Code terminal.

3. Paste the whole master prompt below in one go and press Enter.

4. Approve file changes when Claude asks. It installs packages, builds the site and tests it in a browser. Let it finish.

COPY THIS PROMPT   *paste into Claude Code (the master prompt)*

| Build a one-product website for a cat food brand called "Mochi". The product is "Mochi Crunch", a salmon & chicken dry kibble in a 1.5 kg pink bag. Use React \+ TypeScript \+ Vite \+ Tailwind CSS v4 (@tailwindcss/vite plugin), plus GSAP (with ScrollTrigger and SplitText) and Lenis for motion.Work in this folder. Test everything in a real browser before you say it's done.ASSETS ALREADY IN THIS FOLDER\- hero-cat.mp4: a 1920×1080 video of a fluffy white cartoon cat centred on a hot pink background, looking in different directions (left, right, up, down, centre), possibly with blinks in between.\- image-sources/: pouch.png (transparent bag cutout), kitten-hug.png, pouch-float.png, cat-bowl.png, kibble.png (transparent, three heart-shaped kibble pieces).\- video-sources/: kitten-hug.mp4 and pouch-float.mp4 (5-second clips).Convert images to WebP in public/images (photos \~1200–1600px q80; cutouts keep transparency, trimmed).Split kibble.png into three single transparent pieces: public/images/kibble-one/two/three.webp.Make ping-pong seamless loops of both videos into public/videos (900px wide, H.264, crf 25, no audio, faststart). Keep image-sources and video-sources out of public and add them to .gitignore.If hero-cat.mp4 is HEVC, convert it to H.264 first.BRAND\- Colours: hero pink \#EC2F69, pink \#F2306E, deep pink \#D01655, blush \#FFE6EE, plum text \#3A0B22, soft plum \#6E3A55, yellow accent \#FFD24A. Match the hero page background to the video's pink.\- Font: "Bricolage Grotesque" from Google Fonts (opsz, wdth, wght axes). Headlines use a condensed heavy cut: font-weight 800, font-variation-settings 'wdth' 75, 'opsz' 96, line-height 0.88. Body text in the same family at normal width.\- Tone: short, warm, plain sentences. Sentence case. No all-caps labels.HERO (full screen, the most important part)\- The cat video frames are the background, full-bleed, cover the screen, cat centred, never crop the cat's head (anchor to the top on landscape; on portrait phones anchor the scene to the bottom and fade its top edge into the pink).\- The cat must look toward the mouse cursor (and toward a finger tap on phones).   First ANALYSE the video with ffmpeg \+ Python (numpy/Pillow): extract every frame, find the two eyes in each frame (dark pixels in the face area), compute where the head/eyes point relative to the centre pose, and mark frames where the eyes are closed (blinks).   Then choose the method:   (a) If the video is ONE continuous sweep with no blinks, map the cursor position directly to the video's currentTime (scrub it), with a guard so seeks don't pile up.   (b) If it has several held poses with blinks (most AI videos), export only the useful frames as WebP, cropped to the area around the cat, plus one full background frame (bg.jpg). Write a JSON manifest with each frame's gaze direction. On a \<canvas\> over the background, show the frame whose gaze best matches the cursor direction. Between frames in the same continuous stretch, step through the real in-between frames; across a blink, crossfade in \~170ms. Load the centre and 4 main poses first, then the rest in the background.   Extras: when idle for \~7 seconds, play a slow blink from the video's own blink frames; pause rendering when the hero is off-screen; respect prefers-reduced-motion.\- Text is split around the cat: left "Picky eaters," right "clean bowls." (huge condensed white type, clamp(44px, 5.6vw, 116px)). Under the left word: "Real salmon and chicken in every crunchy heart." and a white pill button "Shop Mochi Crunch" that scrolls to the product section. On phones, stack all of it centred above the cat. Real \<h1\> for screen readers.\- Top bar: "mochi" wordmark left, links "The bag", "What's inside", "Feeding guide", and a white "Bag" pill with a count on the right.SECTION 1: THE BAG (id="product", blush background)\- Left: kitten-hug as a looping video (poster \= the still), rounded 40px, 4:5.\- Right: big "Mochi Crunch" heading; one line of description; three check-mark points ("Real salmon is the first ingredient", "Grain-free, with no artificial colours", "A complete meal for adult cats"); two choice cards "Subscribe & save (10% off, every 4 weeks)" and "One-time"; big price (\$22.49 on subscription, \$24.99 one-time, show the old price struck through); quantity stepper; "Add to bag" button.   Adding shows a small toast and updates the Bag count in the top bar.SECTION 2: WHAT'S INSIDE (id="inside", magenta → deep plum radial gradient, white text)\- Centred heading "What's inside the bag".\- Centre: pouch-float as a looping video. Left: "38% protein" and "0 grains" in huge type. Right: a yellow circle with "1.5 kg bag". Hand-drawn style SVG arrows point from the stats to the bag.\- Below: "Ingredients, in order" as chips with percentages, and "Guaranteed analysis" as four small cards (Protein 38%, Fat 17%, Fibre 3%, Moisture 9%).SECTION 3: HOW MUCH TO FEED (id="feeding", blush)\- Heading "How much to feed"; a white card with a weight slider (2–8 kg), a "Calm and indoors / Busy or outdoors" choice, and results "Each day: X g" and "One bag lasts: Y days".   Formula: kcal/day \= 70 × kg^0.75 × (1.0 calm or 1.3 active); food has 390 kcal/100 g; bag is 1500 g.\- Beside it: cat-bowl photo (3:2, rounded).\- Closing pink banner: "Mochi is waiting by the bowl.", price line, white "Add Mochi Crunch to bag" button, with the transparent bag cutout tilted 8° and overlapping the banner's top-right edge.FOOTER (deep pink): one line of vet advice, section links, and a giant "mochi" wordmark.MOTION (premium, smooth, never bouncy)\- Lenis smooth scroll driven by the GSAP ticker; ScrollTrigger updates on Lenis scroll.\- Page load: hero headline words rise from a mask with a slight blur, then the line and button, then the top bar.\- Hero → product: pin the hero and, while scrolling, shrink it to 0.88 scale with 48px corners and dim it (brightness 1 → 0.72, give GSAP the explicit start value "brightness(1)"), while the product section slides over it with rounded top corners that flatten. Kibble pieces erupt upward from the seam.\- Floating kibble: \~16 real kibble cutouts around the kitten video at random depths (small+soft far away, sharp in the middle, big+blurred up close), some in front of the video and some behind. Each drifts gently forever, moves with scroll (parallax by depth) and with the mouse. Keep them off the kitten's face.\- Between Section 1 and 2: two crossing tilted ribbons (plum and yellow) with marquee text "Real salmon, Real chicken, Crunchy hearts, Grain-free, Made for picky eaters" with small hearts, scrolling in opposite directions and speeding up with scroll velocity.\- Section 2 opens as a growing circle (clip-path circle 6% → 150%) behind the ribbons; the video scales in; arrows draw themselves; "38%" and "1.5" count up; the yellow circle pops in.\- Every heading reveals word by word on scroll; content blocks fade up in sequence; photos unmask upward with a slight zoom-out; the bowl photo has gentle parallax.\- Add to bag fires a burst of kibble pieces from the button. Buttons are subtly magnetic on desktop.\- Kibble rains slowly behind the closing banner; the bag in the banner bobs up and down.\- The footer wordmark rises as you reach the bottom.\- prefers-reduced-motion: no smooth scroll, no pinning, still photos instead of videos, all content visible.QUALITY\- Works on phones (390px wide) with no sideways scrolling.\- Visible keyboard focus, real buttons and labels, alt text on every image.\- Videos play only while on screen.\- Run \`npm run build\` with no errors, then open the site in a browser, scroll through every section on desktop and phone, and fix anything that overlaps or looks broken.\- Never put API keys in code or commit .env files. |

# Deploy to GitHub \+ Vercel

*Three blocks of commands give you a private GitHub repo and a public link you can share.*

❦

| ⚠️  Replace `YOUR-USERNAME` with your GitHub username and `my-product-site` with your project name. After `git status`, make sure `.env.local`, `node_modules`, `image-sources` and `video-sources` are not listed. |
| :---- |

TERMINAL   *paste into Terminal, then press Enter*

| `# 1. Make sure the key file is NOT going to be uploadedgit init -b maingit add -Agit status            # .env.local, node_modules, image-sources, video-sources must NOT be listed# 2. Save and push to a new private GitHub repogit commit -m "My animated product site"gh repo create YOUR-USERNAME/my-product-site --private --source=. --remote=origin --push# 3. Create the Vercel project, connect it to GitHub, and go livevercel link --yes --project my-product-sitevercel --prod --yes` |
| :---- |

Vercel prints your live address, for example `https://my-product-site.vercel.app`. From now on, every `git push` updates the live site.

### Prefer clicking to typing?

1. Go to vercel.com and sign in with GitHub.

2. Click Add New, then Project.

3. Import your repository and leave the settings as they are (Vercel detects Vite).

4. Click Deploy and wait about a minute.

| 💡  To make the GitHub repo public later, run `gh repo edit YOUR-USERNAME/my-product-site --visibility public`. |

—   GOLDEN RULES   —

# 8 Rules to Follow

*Break one of these and something on the page breaks with it.*

❦

| 1 | Make the bag first *Upload that exact bag as the reference for every other photo.* |
| :---: | :---- |
| 2 | Generate one video at a time *Do not queue everything at once.* |
| 3 | Check the codec *Chrome needs H.264. HEVC videos show nothing.* |
| 4 | Loop every short clip *Ping-pong each clip so it never visibly jumps.* |
| 5 | Keep secrets and originals off GitHub `image-sources`*,* `video-sources` *and* `.env.local` *stay in* `.gitignore`*.* |
| 6 | Lowercase names with hyphens *No spaces and no capitals in file names, ever.* |
| 7 | Edit the master prompt first *Your brand, prices and nutrition values, not ours.* |
| 8 | Test at phone width *Check a narrow window before you call it done.* |

 

—   TROUBLESHOOTING   —

# Mistakes We Hit

*So you don't have to.*

❦

| PROBLEM | WHY IT HAPPENED | FIX |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Video shows nothing in Chrome | The file was HEVC (H.265) | Re-encode to H.264 (Step 2\) |
| The cat's look feels jumpy | The AI video had separate poses with blinks | Use the smoother prompt in Step 2, or accept small jumps |
| Double eyes when frames blend | Two frames with the head in different places were crossfaded | Only crossfade across blinks |
| Kie: "aspect\_ratio is not within the range" | Image-to-image does not accept 4:5 | Use 3:4 |
| Kie: "generation with background is temporarily unavailable" | `background` only works at 1K | Leave `background` out for 2K images |
| Hero turns black when the animation starts | GSAP read `filter: none` as `brightness(0)` | Give GSAP an explicit start value: `brightness(1)` |
| Loop jumps at the restart | The last frame does not match the first | Ping-pong loop (Step 4\) |
| Kibble covers the kitten's face on phones | Parallax moved the front pieces too far | Smaller parallax, keep pieces off the centre |
| Huge upload to GitHub | Original PNGs and videos were in the repo | Add them to `.gitignore` (Step 5\) |

# Image Script

*Create scripts/generate-images.mjs in your project, triple-click the box, paste, save. Used by Option B in Step 3\.*

❦

FILE   *scripts/generate-images.mjs*

| ``// Generates the site's product imagery with Kie's GPT Image 2 API.// Usage: KIE_API_KEY in .env.local, then `node scripts/generate-images.mjs [--only name] [--force]`.// The pouch packshot is made first and uploaded, then used as a reference so every scene shows the same pouch.import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'const API = 'https://api.kie.ai/api/v1'const UPLOAD = 'https://kieai.redpandaai.co/api/file-stream-upload'const OUT = new URL('../image-sources/', import.meta.url)mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true })function apiKey() {  if (process.env.KIE_API_KEY) return process.env.KIE_API_KEY  const envFile = new URL('../.env.local', import.meta.url)  if (existsSync(envFile)) {    const match = readFileSync(envFile, 'utf8').match(/^KIE_API_KEY\s*=\s*"?([^"\n]+)"?/m)    if (match) return match[1].trim()  }  throw new Error('KIE_API_KEY is missing. Add it to .env.local as KIE_API_KEY=your-key')}const KEY = apiKey()const auth = { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` }const POUCH = `a matte hot-pink stand-up pouch of premium dry cat food with a white zip top and rounded corners.The front shows a large white lowercase wordmark "mochi" in a bold, condensed, friendly grotesque typeface.Below it, a simple flat illustration of a fluffy white kitten face with big round brown eyes and a tiny smile.Small white text at the bottom reads "Salmon & Chicken Crunch" and "1.5 kg". Clean, modern, premium packaging design`const PINK = 'a seamless hot pink studio backdrop (#EC2F69) with soft, even light and a gentle vignette'const JOBS = [  {    name: 'pouch',    model: 'gpt-image-2-text-to-image',    input: {      prompt: `Studio product photograph of ${POUCH}. The pouch stands upright, facing the camera straight on, softly lit, crisp label, realistic material texture. Isolated on a transparent background, no shadow.`,      aspect_ratio: '2:3',      resolution: '1K',      background: 'transparent',    },  },  {    name: 'kitten-hug',    usesPouch: true,    model: 'gpt-image-2-image-to-image',    input: {      prompt: `Top-down photograph, shot from directly above. A fluffy white kitten lies on its back, eyes closed in a blissful sleepy smile, hugging the pink cat food pouch from the reference image to its chest with both front paws; its pink toe beans on the back paws face the camera and its tail curls to one side. Heart-shaped brown kibble is scattered in a loose halo around the kitten. Background: ${PINK}. Photorealistic, soft natural fur detail, shallow depth of field, advertising photography. Keep the pouch design exactly as in the reference.`,      aspect_ratio: '3:4',      resolution: '2K',    },  },  {    name: 'pouch-float',    usesPouch: true,    model: 'gpt-image-2-image-to-image',    input: {      prompt: `Dynamic advertising photograph. The pink cat food pouch from the reference image floats in mid-air, tilted about 12 degrees, centred. Heart-shaped brown kibble pieces fly around it at different depths: some sharp, some large and blurred in the foreground corners. A fluffy white cat paw reaches in from the top right corner toward the pouch. Background: a rich magenta-to-deep-plum gradient (#EC2F69 fading to #5A0B3A) with soft rim light. Photorealistic, high-end pet food campaign. Keep the pouch design exactly as in the reference.`,      aspect_ratio: '3:4',      resolution: '2K',    },  },  {    name: 'cat-bowl',    usesPouch: true,    model: 'gpt-image-2-image-to-image',    input: {      prompt: `Photograph of a fluffy white cat with big brown eyes happily eating heart-shaped brown kibble from a glossy pale-pink ceramic bowl on the floor. The pink cat food pouch from the reference image stands just behind the bowl, slightly out of focus. A few kibble pieces are scattered on the floor. Background: ${PINK}. Eye-level camera, warm soft light, photorealistic, advertising photography. Keep the pouch design exactly as in the reference.`,      aspect_ratio: '3:2',      resolution: '2K',    },  },  {    name: 'kibble',    model: 'gpt-image-2-text-to-image',    input: {      prompt: 'Three pieces of heart-shaped brown dry cat food kibble, photographed close up, crisp and realistic, slightly different angles, arranged loosely apart from each other. Isolated on a transparent background, no shadow.',      aspect_ratio: '1:1',      resolution: '1K',      background: 'transparent',    },  },]const args = process.argv.slice(2)const only = args.includes('--only') ? args[args.indexOf('--only') + 1] : nullconst force = args.includes('--force')async function json(response) {  const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({}))  if (!response.ok || (body.code && body.code !== 200)) {    throw new Error(`${response.status} ${body.msg ?? JSON.stringify(body)}`)  }  return body}async function createTask(job, inputUrls) {  const input = { ...job.input }  if (inputUrls) input.input_urls = inputUrls  const body = await json(    await fetch(`${API}/jobs/createTask`, {      method: 'POST',      headers: { ...auth, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },      body: JSON.stringify({ model: job.model, input }),    }),  )  return body.data.taskId}async function waitFor(taskId, name) {  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000))    const body = await json(await fetch(`${API}/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=${taskId}`, { headers: auth }))    const { state, resultJson, failMsg } = body.data    if (state === 'success') return JSON.parse(resultJson).resultUrls[0]    if (state === 'fail') throw new Error(`${name} failed: ${failMsg}`)    if (attempt % 6 === 0) console.log(`  ${name}: ${state}…`)  }  throw new Error(`${name} timed out`)}async function download(url, name) {  const response = await fetch(url)  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`download ${name}: ${response.status}`)  const file = new URL(`${name}.png`, OUT)  writeFileSync(file, Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()))  return file}async function upload(file) {  const form = new FormData()  form.append('file', new Blob([readFileSync(file)], { type: 'image/png' }), 'mochi-pouch.png')  form.append('uploadPath', 'mochi')  form.append('fileName', 'mochi-pouch.png')  const body = await json(await fetch(UPLOAD, { method: 'POST', headers: auth, body: form }))  return body.data.fileUrl ?? body.data.downloadUrl}async function run(job, pouchUrl) {  const target = new URL(`${job.name}.png`, OUT)  if (existsSync(target) && !force && only !== job.name) {    console.log(`✓ ${job.name} (already generated)`)    return  }  console.log(`→ ${job.name}`)  const taskId = await createTask(job, job.usesPouch ? [pouchUrl] : null)  const url = await waitFor(taskId, job.name)  await download(url, job.name)  console.log(`✓ ${job.name}`)}const selected = JOBS.filter((job) => !only || job.name === only)const pouchJob = JOBS[0]const pouchFile = new URL('pouch.png', OUT)if (selected.some((job) => job.name === 'pouch') || !existsSync(pouchFile)) await run(pouchJob)const needsPouch = selected.some((job) => job.usesPouch)const pouchUrl = needsPouch ? await upload(pouchFile) : nullconst results = await Promise.allSettled(selected.filter((job) => job.name !== 'pouch').map((job) => run(job, pouchUrl)))results.forEach((r) => r.status === 'rejected' && console.error('✗', r.reason.message))`` |

# Video Script

*Create scripts/generate-videos.mjs in your project, triple-click the box, paste, save. Used by Option B in Step 4\.*

❦

FILE   *scripts/generate-videos.mjs*

| ``// Animates two existing product photos into 5-second clips with Kling 2.6 on Kie.// Usage: KIE_API_KEY in .env.local, then `node scripts/generate-videos.mjs [--only name]`.import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'const API = 'https://api.kie.ai/api/v1'const UPLOAD = 'https://kieai.redpandaai.co/api/file-stream-upload'const DIR = new URL('../video-sources/', import.meta.url)const envFile = new URL('../.env.local', import.meta.url)const KEY =  process.env.KIE_API_KEY ??  (existsSync(envFile) ? readFileSync(envFile, 'utf8').match(/^KIE_API_KEY\s*=\s*"?([^"\n]+)"?/m)?.[1].trim() : null)if (!KEY) throw new Error('KIE_API_KEY is missing from .env.local')const auth = { Authorization: `Bearer ${KEY}` }const JOBS = [  {    name: 'kitten-hug',    prompt:      'Locked-off overhead camera, no camera movement. The fluffy white kitten lying on its back breathes slowly and peacefully, its chest rising and falling, whiskers and ear tips twitching slightly, back paws flexing gently, the tip of its tail curling softly. It keeps hugging the pink bag, eyes closed and content. The kibble and pink background stay completely still. Calm, cozy, subtle, realistic motion.',  },  {    name: 'pouch-float',    prompt:      'Locked-off camera, no zoom or pan. The pink cat food bag floats and bobs gently in mid-air, rotating a few degrees back and forth. The heart-shaped kibble pieces drift slowly upward and tumble in slow motion at different depths. The fluffy white cat paw reaches in playfully and taps toward the bag. Dreamy, smooth, slow, premium advertising motion. Keep the bag label unchanged.',  },]const only = process.argv.includes('--only') ? process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--only') + 1] : nullasync function json(response) {  const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({}))  if (!response.ok || (body.code && body.code !== 200)) throw new Error(`${response.status} ${body.msg ?? JSON.stringify(body)}`)  return body}async function upload(name) {  const form = new FormData()  form.append('file', new Blob([readFileSync(new URL(`${name}.jpg`, DIR))], { type: 'image/jpeg' }), `${name}.jpg`)  form.append('uploadPath', 'mochi')  form.append('fileName', `${name}.jpg`)  const body = await json(await fetch(UPLOAD, { method: 'POST', headers: auth, body: form }))  return body.data.fileUrl ?? body.data.downloadUrl}async function run(job) {  const target = new URL(`${job.name}.mp4`, DIR)  if (existsSync(target) && only !== job.name) return console.log(`✓ ${job.name} (already generated)`)  console.log(`→ ${job.name}`)  const imageUrl = await upload(job.name)  const created = await json(    await fetch(`${API}/jobs/createTask`, {      method: 'POST',      headers: { ...auth, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },      body: JSON.stringify({        model: 'kling-2.6/image-to-video',        input: { prompt: job.prompt, image_urls: [imageUrl], sound: false, duration: '5' },      }),    }),  )  const taskId = created.data.taskId  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 180; attempt++) {    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 6000))    const body = await json(await fetch(`${API}/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=${taskId}`, { headers: auth }))    const { state, resultJson, failMsg } = body.data    if (state === 'fail') throw new Error(`${job.name} failed: ${failMsg}`)    if (state === 'success') {      const url = JSON.parse(resultJson).resultUrls[0]      writeFileSync(target, Buffer.from(await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer()))      return console.log(`✓ ${job.name}`)    }    if (attempt % 10 === 0) console.log(`  ${job.name}: ${state}…`)  }  throw new Error(`${job.name} timed out`)}const results = await Promise.allSettled(JOBS.filter((j) => !only || j.name === only).map(run))results.forEach((r) => r.status === 'rejected' && console.error('✗', r.reason.message))`` |
